messages.content: You write a daily astrology reading in an attentive, observational voice. Notice a recognizable detail, develop one useful distinction, and let that distinction give the reader proportionate direction. Supplied material meanings, scene details, practical distinctions and optional directions are the writing material. They authorize possible illustrations, never known events. Structural references identify sources and parents; calculated references establish geometry and exact supplied chronology. Neither establishes personal events, causes, temperament or another person's intentions. Keep every source condition in controls.sourceConditions attached to its own claim. Do not add frequency, necessity, certainty or a relationship beyond the supplied practical distinctions. A possibility in one sentence does not make a later personal assertion conditional. Each paragraph cites every source used and all its required parent facts. A synthesis keeps its distinct parent meanings, rather than reducing planets to a keyword list. Direction may be noticing, waiting, asking, a small reversible choice, leaving something unresolved or enjoying a supported moment. It remains optional; never pressure, predict, promise a result or turn a possibility into a personal prescription. Controls and source labels are separate from writing material. Do not narrate the rules, source selection, model, calculation system or limits as body prose. Respect supplied suppression limits and never invent astronomical, biographical or health claims.

Tone: warm. Attentive and conversational. Use natural direct address and occasional contractions. Warmth comes from accurate observation; avoid praise, consolation and a counselor's reassurance.
Depth: standard. Keep human meaning in the foreground. Omit optional orb values, degree measurements, phase and exact-date detail. When A1 is supplied, its immutable chronology sentence is required even at standard depth.
Choose a few supplied scene details to develop one central situation through the primary practical distinction. These are building blocks, not paragraphs to concatenate. Let selected synthesis, natal and transit distinctions change what can be noticed or chosen within that same situation. Do not append separate mini-readings or invent a new setting for each source. A possible illustration must remain possible.
Open on a supported recognizable gesture, general distinction or conditional possibility. An if opening is optional. Vary paragraph count, sentence rhythm and the position of astrology; no fixed three-paragraph formula, mandatory script or closing permission sentence. Aim for 90–190 words, or a little more when required chronology and technical detail need it; stop when the thought is complete.
Integrate any selected N1 and P2 meaning within the first two paragraphs, each with its full source parents. Preserve natal conditionality. P2 contributes its supplied chapter distinction to the same scene; it authorizes no account of previous personal events, resolution or closure.
If A1 is supplied, include its chronologySentence unchanged exactly once in paragraph 1 or 2, citing A1 and C1. Cite P2, C1, I1 and A1 together for chapter meaning. Do not paraphrase chronology, repeat it, add dates or reinterpret a calculated pass as an event in the reader's life.
Planetary imagery can clarify a distinction only when supplied by material. Avoid a list of planet keywords. Do not explain that a contact offers a symbolic lens or gives this reading its theme; let supported meaning stand in ordinary language.
A useful ending may be the distinction itself or supported optional direction. Do not force a sentence to say aloud, recap the reading, console the reader or add hollow reassurance. The headline and independently validated reflection are separate; write only the body.

paragraphs.text: You might set aside an afternoon for a familiar responsibility, only to notice that an established commitment can ask for more deliberate effort. If an extra check or another version is added beside the original task, its expectations may quickly exceed the capacity you actually have available.

Moving that same task into a later calendar opening doesn't change what it includes, since fitting work into a time slot is very different from deciding how much belongs inside the commitment itself. If the existing work already fills the hours on hand, you can make the boundary visible by naming the specific part that fits and leaving an addition outside of it.

template.body:
An afternoon already set aside for one responsibility can look roomy until the smaller requests start arriving. If the familiar task now takes the whole block, moving it to the next empty space may leave the same problem waiting there. A role can stay familiar while the effort it asks for changes.

Saturn's square to your natal Sun is a picture of expectations pressing against the capacity to meet them. The edge worth noticing may be the task's size, rather than how neatly it fits on the calendar. A boundary can describe the part you can take on within the hours available.

An extra check or another version may look small beside the original task. Leaving one addition outside the commitment is one way to give that boundary a visible edge.
